rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God's days is meant to stir love and direct yearning toward the Beloved; alternatively, the days are divine self-disclosures in majesty, recalled to inspire fear and obedience.
rows.anchor: بتذكير ذلك ليثور غرامهم ويأخذ بهم نحو الحبيب هيامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are for every believer in the unseen; patience and gratitude are described as two stations of the wayfarer before arrival.
rows.anchor: لكل مؤمن بالايمان الغيبي سد الصبر والشكر على ماقيل مقامان

rows.speaker: الجوزجاني
rows.claim: Gratitude progresses from favor to knowledge, then connection, closeness, and intimacy; gratitude for each stage brings the next.
rows.anchor: لئن شكرتم الاحسان لأزيدنكم المعرفة ولئن شكرتم المعرفة لأزيدنكم الوصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise also means that thanking God for one blessing brings a better blessing; the highest gratitude admits one cannot adequately give thanks.
rows.anchor: لئن شكرتم نعمة لأزيدنكم نعمة خيرا منها وللشكر مراتب

rows.speaker: داود
rows.claim: David asks how he can thank God when gratitude itself is among God's favors; God answers that David has now thanked Him.
rows.anchor: داود عليه السلام قال : يارب كيف أشكرك والشكر من آلائك

rows.speaker: حمدون
rows.claim: Hamdun defines gratitude for a blessing as seeing oneself as an intruder who has no rightful claim to it.
rows.anchor: شكر النعمة أن ترى نفسك فيها طفيليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There can be no doubt about God, who is manifest in the horizons and in human selves.
rows.anchor: أنه سبحانه لاشك فيه لأنه الظاهر في الآفاق والأنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the Originator of the heavens and earth, bringing them into existence and manifesting them from nonbeing.
rows.anchor: موجدهما ومظهرهما من كتم العدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to forgiveness is read mystically as God's light covering the darkness of the hearers' attributes, so certainty leaves no room for doubt; the appointed term follows their capacity for felicity.
rows.anchor: ليستر بنوره سبحانه ظلمات حجب صفاتكم فلا تشكون فيه عند جلية اليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers accept that they share human nature with their people, but God's favor uniquely equips the messengers for prophethood; the same answer applies to deniers of eminent shaykhs.
rows.anchor: سلموا لهم المشاركة في الجنس وجعلوا الموجب لاختصاصهم بالنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only by God's leave can messengers bring a clear sign; the same answer addresses people who demand a saintly miracle merely out of obstinacy.
rows.anchor: جواب عن قول أولئك : ( فأتونا بسلطان مبين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith entails reliance on God, understood as becoming still beneath divine decrees; another definition places the heart in lordship and the body in servitude, so the reliant wants only what God wills.
rows.anchor: لأن الايمان يقتضي التوكل وهو الخمود تحت الموارد وفسره بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The perfected person dislikes displaying miracles; the mystics discuss this issue in detail.
rows.anchor: وفسره بعضهم بأنه طرح القلب في الربوبية والبدن في العبودية فالمتوكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some mystics distinguish three unveilings: bodily death, voluntary death that leaves the ego's attributes for the heart, and final passage beyond selfhood into true unity.
rows.anchor: فبروز عند القيامة الصغرى بموت الجسد وبروز عند القيامة الوسطى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret the weak and arrogant disputants as appearing through the Mahdi, who distinguishes the people of Paradise from those of the Fire when God's judgment saves the blessed and destroys the wretched.
rows.anchor: فهو بوجود المهدي القائم بالحق الفارق بين أهل الجنة والنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mystics interpret Satan as the faculty of illusion, and sometimes as the commanding lower self; others retain the ordinary scriptural Satan.
rows.anchor: وفسروا الشيطان بالوهم وقد يفسرونه في بعض المواضع بالنفس الأمارة

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says that blaming oneself is associating a partner with God, since the speaker sees another actor where only God exists.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا يشير كلام الواسطي حيث قال : من لام نفسه فقد أشرك

rows.speaker: محمد بن حامد
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Hamid instead says the lower self is the proper object of blame, and anyone who never reproaches it has ruined it.
rows.anchor: النفس محل كل لائمة فمن لم يلم نفسه على الدوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The latter counsel is supported by the sacred report that people should praise God for good and blame only themselves for evil; the author asks readers to reflect on its tension with the mystics' claim.
rows.anchor: ماصح في الحديث القدسي ياعبادي إنما هي أعمالكم أحصيها لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the people of spiritual election and nearness are greeted by their Lord, while the obedient people of ranked degrees are greeted by angels.
rows.anchor: منهم من يحييهم ربهم وهم أهل الصفوة والقربة ومنهم من يحييهم الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beloved's greeting to the one who loves him is especially sweet and delightful to the heart.
rows.anchor: أطيب سلام المحبوب على محبه وما ألذه على قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good word is interpreted as the declaration of divine unity planted by God in the garden of spirits; its root is divinely sustained, while its branches, leaves, and fruit signify nearness, love, longing, care, servitude, and knowledge of divine lights.
rows.anchor: إشارة كما قيل إلى كلمة التوحيد التي غرسها الحق في ارض بساتين الارواح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the good word the purified soul, rooted in tranquillity and sound conviction and bearing fruits of knowledge, wisdom, and realities through God's facilitation.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الكلمة الطيبة النفس الطيبة أصلها ثابت بالاطمئنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bad word signifies either unbelief or an impure soul; Ja'far al-Sadiq maps its tree to desires, its soil to selves, water to hopes, leaves to laziness, fruit to sins, and end to the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقال جعفر الصادق رضي الله تعالى عنه : الشجرة الخبيثة الشهوات وارضها النفوس

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: God steadies believers in worldly life upon faith and in the next life upon a truthful answer to the Merciful.
rows.anchor: قال الصادق رضي الله تعالى عنه : يثبتهم في الحياة الدنيا على الايمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret the firm word as God's eternal decree, which fixes the believers in their honored standing in both worlds because His unchanging decree settled it from eternity.
rows.anchor: وجعل بعضهم القول الثابت قوله سبحانه وحكمه الأزلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God misguides wrongdoers in both lives because of their ill preparedness.
rows.anchor: في الحياتين لسوء استعدادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing exchanged for unbelief is original guidance and innate light, while unbelief is concealment and error; their followers are brought into ruin and deprivation.
rows.anchor: من الهداية الاصلية والنور الفطري ( كفرا ) احتجابا وضلالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly possessions and desires made into rivals are what their owners love as they love God, and their example misleads whoever notices and turns toward them.
rows.anchor: من متاع الدنيا ومشتهياتها التي يحبونها كحب الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens signify spirits, earth bodies, the highest heaven the holy realm, and its water knowledge; fruits are wisdom and virtues that nourish the heart.
rows.anchor: أي سموات الارواح ( والأرض ) أي أرض الاجساد ( وأنزل من السماء ) أي سماء عالم القدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ships signify intellects sailing the sea of divine favors and secrets; rivers are streams of knowledge, sun the spirit, moon the heart, and their motion spiritual unveiling and witnessing.
rows.anchor: وسخر لكم الفلك ) أي فلك العقول ( لتجري في البحر ) أي بحر آلائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night represents the darkness of the lower self's attributes, while day is the spirit's light for worldly and next-worldly livelihood, rest, and illumination.
rows.anchor: ليل ظلمة صفات النفس ( والنهار ) نهار نور الروح لطلب المعاش والمعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives each thing requested through the tongue of one's preparedness, since such a request is not denied; His prior and later blessings cannot be counted because they are infinite.
rows.anchor: بلسان الاستعداد فان المسؤل بذلك لايمنع ( وإن تعدوا نعمة الله )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person wrongs God by withholding His due, or wrongs himself by nullifying preparedness, placing its light in nature's darkness, and putting what should endure in what perishes; ingratitude follows heedlessness of blessings.
rows.anchor: ينقص حق الله تعالى أو حق نفسه بابطال الاستعداد أو يضع نور الاستعداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading says a person wrongs himself by imagining that gratitude could repay God's blessings, and is ungrateful because he is veiled from seeing grace at every beginning and end.
rows.anchor: حيث يظن أن شكره يقابل نعمه تعالى كفار محجوب عن رؤية الفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and sons are the worldly adornments about which the unbelieving brother boasted; wealth precedes sons because it is more fundamentally tied to adornment and support.
rows.anchor: بيان لشأن ما كانوا يفتخرون به من محسنات الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth adorns and supports parents and children alike at all times, while sons adorn and support only those who become parents; wealth sustains individual life, sons the species, and wealth is more urgently needed and comes first.
rows.anchor: وعمومه بالنسبة إلى الإفراد والأوقات فإنه زينة وممد لكل أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth can be an adornment without sons, but sons without wealth leave a person in distress; ornament is a verbal noun transferred to the thing used for adornment for emphasis.
rows.anchor: ولأنه زينة بدونهم من غير عكس فإن من له بنون بلا مال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive ties these ornaments specifically to worldly life; alternatively it means ornaments found in worldly life, whose rapid decay makes their ornaments perish even sooner.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن تكون على معنى في والمعنى أن ما يفتخرون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's implicit argument is that worldly life quickly vanishes, so its ornaments do too, and a wise person should not boast of things that vanish quickly.
rows.anchor: وكل ما كان سريع الزوال يقبح بالعاقل أن يفتخر به

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet urges believers to increase the enduring good deeds, naming takbir, tahlil, tasbih, tahmid, and saying there is no power or strength except through God; reported from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال استكثروا من الباقيات الصالحات

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet identifies the enduring deeds as glorifying, praising, affirming God's oneness, magnifying God, and declaring there is no power or strength except through God; they erase sins like a tree sheds leaves and are Paradise's treasures, in a report from Abu al-Darda.
rows.anchor: سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second report from Ibn Abbas identifies the enduring deeds with the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: في رواية أخرى عنه تفسيرها بالصلوات الخمس وأخرج ابن مردويه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas interprets them as all good deeds.
rows.anchor: في رواية أخرى عنه أيضا تفسيرها بجميع أعمال الحسنات وفي معناه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the enduring deeds are everything done seeking God's approval.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة أنها كل ما أريد به وجه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the enduring deeds as good intentions.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن وابن عطاء أنها النيات الصالحة

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata also interprets the enduring deeds as good intentions.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن وابن عطاء أنها النيات الصالحة

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari and others select Ibn Abbas's report that the phrase covers all good deeds, a general meaning that includes the specific interpretations in the reports.
rows.anchor: واختار الطبري وغيره ما في الرواية الأخيرة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji argues that narrower explanations are examples of the general category; al-Alusi questions this because the Prophet's wording these are implies restriction after naming specific acts.
rows.anchor: وادعى الخفاجي أن كل ما ذكر في تفسيرها غير العام ذكر على طريق التمثيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enduring is an adjective of omitted words or deeds, and their reward is what endures; alternatively the adjective is attached by ellipsis to a deleted noun.
rows.anchor: فالباقيات صفة لمقدر كالكلمات أو الأعمال وإسناد الباقيات إلى ذلك مجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poor believers who call on God morning and evening seeking His face are included first of all; the passage honors them and lowers the status of their detractors.
rows.anchor: وكذا تدخل أعمال فقراء المؤمنين الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These deeds are better with God in the afterlife, where their excellence appears; alternatively with God means according to His judgment, and the comparison is not that deeds outrank wealth in their shared worldly basis.
rows.anchor: أي في الآخرة وهو بيان لما يظهر فيه آثار خيريتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thawaban means reward and recompense, or alternatively benefit.
rows.anchor: جزاء وأجرا وقيل نفعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good deeds are better hope because they realize in the afterlife what their doer hopes for, whereas wealth and sons do not; repeating better emphasizes the point or signals distinct grounds of superiority.
rows.anchor: حيث ينال بها صاحبها في الآخرة ما يؤمله بها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening is a new divine statement completing the description of the greatest losers and specifying its referents; it is not included within the preceding command.
rows.anchor: كلام مستأنف من جنابه تعالى مسوق لتكميل تعريف الأخسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejected signs are God's proofs calling to monotheism, both transmitted and rational; another view limits them to the Quran, but the author prefers the broader reading.
rows.anchor: بدلائله سبحانه الداعية إلى التوحيد الشاملة للسمعية والعقلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators take meeting God as a metonym for resurrection, gathering, and subsequent afterlife events; the literal meeting is not intended.
rows.anchor: والأكثرون على أنه كناية عن البعث والحشر وما يتبع ذلك من أمور الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative interpretation supplies an omitted word to mean meeting God's punishment, which the author deems unsound.
rows.anchor: أي لقاء عذابه تعالى وليس بذاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Abu al-Sammal read the bāʾ in faḥabiṭat with fatḥa rather than the usual kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وأبو السمال بفتحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ marks the consequence of disbelief in God's signs and meeting Him, and the deeds in question are wholly nullified.
rows.anchor: أي فحبطت لذلك ( أعمالهم ( المعهودة حبوطا كليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of weight means God will disdain and disregard them, since care and esteem depend on righteous works that have been entirely nullified.
rows.anchor: فنزدري بهم ونحتقرهم ولا نجعل لهم مقدارا واعتبارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, no scales are set for their deeds because the deeds became dust; the author prefers the first interpretation because the second merely repeats their nullification.
rows.anchor: أو لا نضع لأجل وزن أعمالهم ميزانا لأنها قد حبطت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred reading is not a Mu'tazilite position; the objection that contempt arises from disbelief rather than nullification is, the author says, caused by heedlessness.
rows.anchor: وليس من الاعتزال في شيء وقرأ مجاهد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ubayd ibn Umayr read the verb as third-person singular, because God's signs are mentioned immediately before it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وعبيد بن عمير ( فلا يقيم ) بالياء

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr also has a reading with fatḥa on the imperfect prefix, treating qāma as transitive.
rows.anchor: وعند عبيد أيضا ( فلا يقيم ) بفتح ياء المضارعة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, Ibn Muhaysin, and Yaqub also read an intransitive verb, with weight as its subject: no weight stands for them on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد وابن محيصن ويعقوب بخلاف عنهم ( فلا يقوم لهم يوم القيامة وزن )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time clause most plausibly attaches to the preceding noun for the revealed discourse, not to that noun if it simply means speech, since a substantive cannot govern it; telling the story is more fitting than describing its telling.
rows.anchor: والاظهر أنه اسم لما ذكر لأنه هو المعروف مع أن وصف القصة بالاتيان أولى

rows.speaker: الشريف
rows.claim: Al-Sharif transmits that story, account, report, and news may govern adverbial clauses even without a verbal meaning because they imply occurrence.
rows.anchor: نقل الشريف عن بعضهم أن القصة والحديث والخبر والنبا يجوز اعمالها في الظروف خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parses make the clause modify an omitted later event or an omitted earlier command to remember the time Musa saw the fire.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون ظرفا لمضمر مؤخر أي حين رأى نارا كان كيت وكيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says Musa asked Shuayb to leave Midian for Egypt to visit his mother and brother after a long absence, hoping the old case would be forgotten; Shuayb permitted him.
rows.anchor: استاذن شعيبا عليه السلام في الخروج من مدين إلى مصر لزيارة امه واخيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musa was jealous and traveled with his family without a caravan so his wife would not be seen; she rode a donkey with household goods while he drove sheep and avoided the usual road for fear of Syrian rulers.
rows.anchor: وكان عليه السلام رجلا غيورا فخرج بأهله ولم يصحب رفقة لئلا ترى امرأته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Wadi Tuwa west of the mountain, on a dark snowy Friday night, his wife bore a son; Musa had lost the way, his flock had scattered, there was no water, and his flint would not spark before he saw fire to the left.
rows.anchor: ولد له ابن في ليلة مظلمة شاتية مثلجة وكانت ليلة الجمعه وقد ضل الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musa tells his family to stay so they will not follow him to the fire as people commonly do, not because he fears they will relocate elsewhere.
rows.anchor: أمرهم عليه السلام بذلك لئلا يتبعوه فيما عزم عليه من الذهاب إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural address may include wife, child, and servant, or the wife alone, with plural explained by the word family or by honorific usage.
rows.anchor: والخطاب قيل : للمرأة والولد والخادم وقيل : للمرأة وحدها والجمع

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-A'mash, Talha, Hamza, and one transmission from Nafi read the hāʾ in li-ahli as damma.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وطلحة وحمزة ونافع في رواية ( ﴿ لأهله امكثوا ﴾ ) بضم الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anastu means seeing something clearly and without doubt; related explanations connect it with the eye's pupil, the opposite of jinn, reassuring sight, or simply finding something.
rows.anchor: أي ابصرتها ابصارا بينا لا شبهة فيه ومن ذلك انسان العين

rows.speaker: الحارث بن حلزة
rows.claim: Al-Harith ibn Hilliza's line uses anastu to witness the sense of noticing or seeing.
rows.anchor: قال الحرث بن حلزة : آنست نبأة وقد راعها القن اص يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement explains both the command and its content; inna confirms the certain sight to reassure his family, although they had shown neither doubt nor denial.
rows.anchor: والجملة تعليل للأمر والمامور به ولما كان الايناس مقطوعا متيقنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A qabas is a flame carried on the end of a stick, a passive form meaning something kindled; it is the same as a flame-brand and the jadwah elsewhere, not an ember.
rows.anchor: بشعلة مقتبسة تكون على رأس عود ونحوه ففعل بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows min-ha to attach directly to the verb or to an omitted circumstantial phrase describing the firebrand.
rows.anchor: على ما قاله أبو البقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance may mean a guide to the path, a verbal noun used for its agent, a guide possessing guidance by ellipsis, or simply guidance metonymically for finding a guide.
rows.anchor: هاديا يدلنى على الطريق على أنه مصدر سمى به الفاعل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Musa wanted someone to guide him to water, since he had lost it.
rows.anchor: وعن الزجاج أن المراد هاديا يدلنى على الماء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada interpret guidance as direction to the paths of religion, since the minds of the righteous remain occupied with religious purposes; al-Alusi calls this far-fetched given the family-consoling narrative and the parallel wording in 28:29.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد وقتادة أن المراد هاديا يهدينى إلى ابواب الدين

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa prefers spelling hudan with alif and no imala; those who incline it explain it by tanwin resembling a lexical ending, by retaining the lexical ending without tanwin, or by a pausal form used in all cases.
rows.anchor: الجيد أن تكتب بالالف ولا تمال لا الالف بدل التنوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aw prevents exclusion rather than combining both possibilities; ala retains its basic sense of elevation, which became idiomatic for a nearby place close beside the fire.
rows.anchor: وكلمة أو لمنع الخلو دون الجمع وعل على بابها من الاستعلاء

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh explains the preposition bi in marartu bi-Zayd as contact with a place close to him, supporting the local use of ala.
rows.anchor: كما قال سيبويه في مررت بزيد : أنه لصوق بمكان يقرب منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians treat the phrase as a circumstantial description of a guide, moved before its noun: a guide or guidance near the fire, meaning someone to help them warm themselves.
rows.anchor: وقال غير واحد : أن الجار والمجرور في موقع الحال من ( هدى )

rows.speaker: الأنباري
rows.claim: Al-Anbari proposes that ala means at, with, or by, but the author sees no need for these substitutions.
rows.anchor: وعن الأنبارى أن على ههنا بمعنى عند أو بمعنى مع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse names the fire rather than using a pronoun to explain why guidance might be found there, since people are commonly present around a fire.
rows.anchor: وصدرت الجملة بكلمة الترجى لما أن الآيتان وما عطف عليه ليسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression of hope reflects two anticipated possibilities, not certain outcomes; syntactically it may be a rationale for the command, the subject's state as he goes, or an adjective of fire, though the last is rejected.
rows.anchor: أما علة لفعل قد حذف ثقة بما يدل عليه من الأمر بالمكث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating the whole clause of hope as an adjective of fire is defended by comparison to a poetic line, but the author says the analysis is flawed.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هى صفة لنارا ومتى جاز جعل جملة الترجى صلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal turns from the denial that God intends play to the positive claim that His way is to make serious truth overcome play-like falsehood; this point leads into the coming threat.
rows.anchor: إضراب على اتخاذ اللهو واللعب بل عن إرادة الإتخاذ كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the truth with the Quran and falsehood with Satan.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد أن الحق القرآن والباطل الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes truth the proof and falsehood their claims and their description of God with attributes such as having a child; the author prefers the general reading.
rows.anchor: وقيل الحق الحجة والباطل شبههم ووصفهم الله تعالى بغير صفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadhf originally means a forceful, distant throw, and is metaphorically used for bringing truth against falsehood.
rows.anchor: وأصل القذف الرمي البعيد كما قال الراغب وهو مستلزم لصلابة الرمي

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib explains qadhf as distant throwing, entailing a hard impact.
rows.anchor: كما قال الراغب وهو مستلزم لصلابة الرمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Damagha means completely destroying; its original sense is cracking a soft, hollow object, extended metaphorically to annihilation.
rows.anchor: أي يمحقه بالكلية كما فعلنا بأهل القرى المحكمة وأصل الدمغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image may be a simile of a hard body thrown on a soft brain to crush it, suggesting truth's height and falsehood's lowliness; alternatively it is a hidden metaphor comparing truth and falsehood to those bodies, but the author prefers the full simile.
rows.anchor: وجوز أيضا أن يكون استعارة مكنية بتشبيه الحق بشيء صلب

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: Isa ibn Umar reads the verb after fa in the subjunctive; the author notes grammarians reject this construction here because fa does not govern it, and the usual exceptional responses do not apply.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى ابن عمر ( فيدمغه ) بالنصب وضعف بأن ما بعد الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic parallel is disputed: the final verb may be an indicative reinforced by a light emphatic nūn, stopped on with alif; this explanation is considered weak, making the verse's subjunctive reading weaker still.
rows.anchor: سأترك منزلي لبني تميم وألحق بالحجاز فأستريحا

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa takes the subjunctive reading as coordinated with al-haqq, yielding the sense that God casts truth and thereby destroys falsehood.
rows.anchor: والعطف على هذه القراءة على الحق عند أبي البقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A scholar instead compares the coordination to giving hay and cold water; the author prefers coordination with the underlying sense, doing the throwing and then the crushing.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض الأفاضل أنه لو جعل من قبيل علفتها تبنا وماء بارد أصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with damma on both mīm and ghayn in yadmaghuhu is also transmitted.
rows.anchor: وقريء ( فيدمغه ) بضم الميم والغين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sudden particle and nominal clause in fa-idha huwa zahiq stress the speed and completeness of falsehood's disappearance, as if it had never existed.
rows.anchor: وفي إذا الفجائية والجملة الإسمية من الدلالة على كمال المسارعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is for Quraysh or all Arab unbelievers: they too face punishment like those earlier communities.
rows.anchor: وعيد لقريش أو لجميع الكفار من العرب بأن لهم أيضا مثل مالأولئك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean because of what you describe, describeable things, or that the ruin itself comes from their descriptions; ma may be a verbal noun, relative pronoun, or adjective.
rows.anchor: وما إما مصدرية أو موصولة أو موصوفة أي ومستقر لكم الويل والهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment is due to attributing to God what does not befit Him, such as a child, and the address is plainly directed to the unbelievers just mentioned.
rows.anchor: من أجل وصفكم له تعالى بما لا يليق بشأنه الجليل تعالى شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is far-fetched to take the address as turning from absent people to the former inhabitants of ruined towns, based on what their plea had been.
rows.anchor: وأبعد كل البعد من قال : إنه خطاب لأهل القرى على طريق الإلتفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about worshipping other than God may be a new sentence exposing another fault, explaining the scale of the loss, or a circumstantial clause from the person who turned away, with the preceding material parenthetical.
rows.anchor: قيل استئناف نافع عليه بعض قبائحه وقيل استئناف مبين لعظم الخسران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These readings make the verse unlikely to describe a Jew, since Jews do not worship idols even though they took rabbis and monks as lords.
rows.anchor: فهو يبعد كون الآية في أحد من اليهود لأنهم لا يدعون الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objects are apparently idols; supplication means worshipping, beyond God, what cannot harm if left unserved or benefit if worshipped.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المدعو الأصنام لمكان ما في قوله تعالى ( ما لا يضره وما لا ينفعه (

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, supplication means calling upon a lifeless thing to rescue the caller from affliction, although it cannot harm or benefit; repeating ma indicates an inanimate object.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يراد بالدعاء النداء أي ينادي لأجل تخليصه مما أصابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Far error is a metaphor for wandering far into a wilderness, away from the right path.
rows.anchor: عن الحق والهدى مستعار من ضلال من أبعد في التيه ضالا عن الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening says that Shuayb spoke to them but does not call him their brother.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل أخوهم وقيل ( الأيكة ) الشجر الملتف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify the wood as a thicket of interwoven trees, including the dawma tree; alternatively, al-ayka is the entire country like Mecca and Bakka, and on either view its people are distinct from Madyan, despite an unusual report from Ibn Abbas equating them.
rows.anchor: وقيل ( الأيكة ) الشجر الملتف وكان شجرهم الدوم وهو المقل

rows.speaker: الحرميان
rows.claim: The two readers of the Haramain and Ibn Amir read layka with a fatḥa on lām and no alif, treating it as a diptote here and in Sad.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحرميان وابن عامر ( ليكة ) بلام مفتوحة بعدها ياء بغير الف

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says an exegesis book calls Layka the name of a settlement.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : وجدنا في بعض كتب التفسير ان ( ليكة ) اسم للقرية

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says readers using the accusative mistakenly take Layka, written without alif in the codex, as a place name; the codex may spell these two occurrences phonetically, as in the treatment of other forms, while the story is one and Layka is unknown.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشاف من قرأ بالنصب وزعم أن ( ليكة ) بوزن ليلة اسماسم بلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's response calls the claim unsupported: the reading is among the seven and is mutawatir, with a further report from a tafsir book.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بانه دعوى من غير ثبت وكفى ثبتا للمخالف ثبوت القراءة في السبعة

rows.speaker: البخاري
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari's Sahih has both forms, al-Ayka and Layka, glossed as the thicket.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري في صحيحه 0 الأيكة ) وليكة الغيضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the Arabic root l-y-k is unattested, the word may be foreign; non-Arabic roots often differ, and the name can be diptote for being proper, foreign, and feminine.
rows.anchor: إن صح لايضر وتكون الكلمة عجمية ومواد كلام العجم مخالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says denying this mutawatir reading approaches apostasy, noting that al-Mubarrad, Ibn Qutayba, al-Zajjaj, al-Farisi, and al-Nahhas preceded al-Zamakhshari in rejecting it.
rows.anchor: انكار الزمخشري صحة هذه القراءة يقرب من الردة والعياذ بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Layka is also read with the hamza deleted and its vowel shifted onto lām, and is written according to its pronunciation, unlike the spelling with hamza.
rows.anchor: وقريء ( ليكة ) بحذف الهمزة والقاء حركتها على اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being among those who cause loss means shortchanging people's rights through deficient measures.
rows.anchor: أي حقوق الناس بالتطفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic construction may intensify the prohibition; alternatively, as with the prohibition on doubled usury, no restrictive implication is drawn. Either way it reinforces the prior command.
rows.anchor: ولعل المبالغة المستفاد من التركيب متوجهة إلى النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following order to weigh concerns goods measured by weight.
rows.anchor: المذكور تأكيد للامر السابق عليه ( وزنوا ( الموزونات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musa completed the term agreed with Shuayb, and the author takes it to be the latter term, citing Ibn Mardawayh from Muqsim through al-Hasan ibn Ali.
rows.anchor: أي أتم المدة المضروبة لما أراد شعيب منه والمراد به الأجل الآخر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Musa fulfilled the longer and better of the two terms, because God's Messenger keeps his word; Bukhari and others transmit this answer.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه سئل أي الأجلين قضى موسى عليه السلام فقال : قضى أكثرهما وأطيبهما

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: A report through Abu Sa'id says that after the Prophet and successive angels each defer the answer, God declares that Musa fulfilled the more complete and better term, ten years; the author gives the extended chain but no grading.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري أن رجلا سأله أي الأجلين قضى موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ is resumptive: he made the two contracts, undertook the work, and when he completed the term, set out with his family.
rows.anchor: فصيحة أي فعقد العقدين وباشر موسى ما أريد منه فلما أتم الاجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view has Musa travel toward Egypt, with Shuayb's permission, to visit his mother, brother, sister, and relatives because the long absence made him think the old case forgotten; another has him go toward Jerusalem, which the author considers less likely.
rows.anchor: قيل : نحو مصر باذن من شعيب عليه السلام لزيارة والدته وأخيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anisa originally means perception and is broader than sight; al-Zamakhshari defines it as clear, unambiguous seeing, linking humans to visibility and jinn to concealment, while another view means seeing what is comforting.
rows.anchor: وأصل الايناس على ما قيل الاحساس فيكون أعم من الابصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some mystics say what Musa saw was real light, called fire because he thought it was fire; others say it had the appearance of actual fire but its reality lay beyond reason.
rows.anchor: استظهر بعضهم أن المبصر كان نورا حقيقيا إلا أنه عبر عنه بالنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His family may have been wife and servant, or wife and two sons Gershom and Eliezer born during his stay; the latter requires additional years after the contract if he did not consummate the marriage until afterward.
rows.anchor: كان معه عليه السلام على قول امرأته وخادم ويخاطب الاثنان بصيغة الجمع

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says Musa's child was born on the road on the night he noticed the fire.
rows.anchor: وعن وهب أنه عليه السلام ولد له ولد في الطريق ليلة إيناس النار

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan describes a winter journey on an unfamiliar route to avoid Syrian rulers, with Musa's pregnant wife unsure when she would deliver; his jealousy made them alternate between the caravan at night and separation by day, and after losing the route in a dark, freezing, snowy night she went into labor, his flint failed, and they saw a distant fire.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه السلام خرج بأهله وماله في فصل الشتاء وأخذ على غير الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He promises news about the road because the family had lost their way; the sentence explains why he tells them to wait.
rows.anchor: بخبر ( أي بخبر الطريق بأن أجد عندها من يخبرني به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jadwah may be a thick piece of wood with fire at its end or without it, as illustrated by two poems; God's words from the fire clarify the kind meant and intensify it by treating the brand as fire itself.
rows.anchor: أي عود غليظ سواء كان في رأسه نار كما في قوله

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines a jadwah as what remains of wood after it has burned.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب : الجذوة ما يبقى من الحطب بعد الالتهاب

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan defines it as a piece of wood containing fire but without a flame.
rows.anchor: وفي معناه قول أبي حيان : عود فيه نار بلا لهب

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says it is a stick of wood containing fire.
rows.anchor: عن أبن زيد قال : هي عود من حطب فيه النار

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the jadwah was the base of a tree with fire at its tip; on this reading min marks the source, and the fire is the one Musa had already noticed.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة أنها أصل شجرة في طرفها النار قيل : فتكون من على هذا للابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce jadwah with kasra on jīm; al-A'mash, Talha, Abu Haywa, and Hamza use damma.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأكثر ( جذوة ) بكسر الجيم والاعمش وطلحة وأبو حيوة وحمزة بضمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taṣṭalūn means that they warm themselves, proving they were suffering from cold.
rows.anchor: تستدفئون وتتسخنون بها وفيه دليل على أنهم أصابهم برد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This standalone statement urges exclusive worship and migration for God's sake: worldly life does not last, and the afterlife is the place of recompense.
rows.anchor: جملة مستأنفة جيء بها حثا على إخلاص العبادة والهجرة لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every soul must experience death and separation from its body; everyone then returns to God's judgment and recompense according to deeds, so preparation is necessary.
rows.anchor: أي كل نفس من النفوس واجدة مرارة الموت ومفارقة البدن البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing a soul as tasting death is a metaphor comparing death to something bitter, and the participle rather than a verb of tasting stresses certainty; thumma signals temporal or ranked delay.
rows.anchor: إستعارة لتشبيه الموت بأمر كريه الطعم مره والعدول عن تذوق الموت

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abu Haywa reads dhāiqatun with nunation and al-mawta in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة ( ذائقة ) بالتنوين ( الموت ) بالنصب

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reads turjaʿūn in the active voice.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه ( ترجعون ) مبنيا للفاعل

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: Asim transmits yarjiʿūn with the third-person yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وروى عاصم ( يرجعون ) بياء الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lanubawwi'annahum means settling them permanently; the oath and its answer together form the predicate of alladhina, against Tha'lab's ban on an oath and its answer serving as a predicate.
rows.anchor: أي لننزلنهم على وجه الإقامة وجملة القسم وجوابه خبر المبتدأ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the chambers are elevated halls and splendid palaces of pearl, beryl, and ruby; ghurafan is the second object of the verb.
rows.anchor: أي علالي وقصورا جليلة لا قصور فيها وهي على ما روى عن إبن عباس

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali, Abdullah, al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym, Ibn Waththab, Talha, Zayd ibn Ali, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read lanuthwiyannahum from thawā, meaning to reside; ghurafan may be its object, governed by an omitted preposition, or an extended locative accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وعبدالله والربيع بن خيثم

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Amir reads ghurufan with a damma on rāʾ.
rows.anchor: وروى عن إبن عامر أنه قرأ ( غرفا ) بضم الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The river clause describes the chambers, while abiding in them refers either to the chambers or to Paradise.
rows.anchor: صفة لغرفا ( خالدين فيها ( أي في الغرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: How excellent is the workers' wage praises their good works, with its specific referent omitted; alternatively, the distinguishing noun is omitted and the phrase means an excellent wage is the wage of workers.
rows.anchor: أي الأعمال الصالحة والمخصوص بالمدح محذوف ثقة بدلالة ما قبله

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب
rows.claim: Ibn Waththab adds fa in fa-niʿma to signal sequence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ إبن وثاب ( فنعم ) بفاء الترتيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhina ṣabarū may modify the workers, be the predicate of an omitted subject, or be an accusative of praise.
rows.anchor: صفة للعاملين أو خبر مبتدأ محذوف أو نصب على المدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their patience is through unbelievers' abuse, the hardships of migration, and other trials; they rely on God alone in all they do and leave undone.
rows.anchor: صبروا على أذية المشركين وشدائد المهاجرة وغير ذلك من المحن والمشاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since their hearts are sealed, the Prophet is to endure their false claims and evil acts; God's promise to grant victory, manifest the religion, and exalt truth must be fulfilled.
rows.anchor: فأصبر على مكارههم من الأقوال الباطلة والأفعال السيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La yastakhiffannaka means do not let their denial and abuse make you light and anxious; even accusations that the messengers are liars are unsurprising from doubters. Another interpretation is that they do not believe the promise, which the author dismisses.
rows.anchor: لا يحملنك على الخفة والقلق ( الذين لا يوقنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the plural subject is grammatically addressed to others, the prohibition is directed to the Prophet, like the idiom do not let me see you here; it means not to grieve fearfully over them.
rows.anchor: والحمل وإن كان لغيره صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم لكن النهي راجع إليه

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq and Yaqub read yastahiqqannaka with ḥāʾ and qāf, from istihqāq: do not let them tempt you and win you over until they are more entitled to you than believers; on this reading the prohibition addresses the community because the Prophet is protected.
rows.anchor: وقرأ إبن أبي إسحاق ويعقوب ( ولا يستحقنك ) بحاء مهملة وقاف

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: The majority geminate the final nūn; Ibn Abi Abla and Yaqub lighten it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بتشديد النون وخففها إبن أبي عبلة ويعقوب

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report from Ali says that a Kharijite called to him during dawn prayer with the warning that associating partners would nullify one's deeds; Ali answered from the verse, be patient, for God's promise is true, and do not let the uncertain unsettle you. The report is transmitted by Ibn Abi Shayba and others.
rows.anchor: عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أن رجلا من الخوارج ناداه وهو في صلاة الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi treats Ali's answer, spoken during prayer, as an apt response from the Prophet's brother and the gate of the city of knowledge.
rows.anchor: ولا بدع في هذا الجواب من باب مدينة العلم وأخى رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an esoteric reading, the letters alif, lam, and mim point respectively to believers' familiar nature, unbelievers' baseness, and the Lord's forgiveness; Rome signifies the heart, Persia the lower self, and believers the spirit, secret, and intellect. Their struggle alternates as the seeking heart and lower self overcome one another over a few years, with the spirit, secret, and intellect rejoicing when God grants victory.
rows.anchor: الألف إشارة إلى ألفة طبع المؤمنين واللام إلى لؤم طبع الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who know only outward worldly life are veiled people who grasp sensory appearances; things also have an inner aspect grasped by reason, and a level beyond reason known through divine influx and purification, which reason can accept without deriving it.
rows.anchor: فيه إشارة إلى حال المحجوبين ووقوفهم على ظواهر الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author disputes the claim that one must pass through outward forms to reach inward meaning: inward knowledge may arrive without that route, and this is higher.
rows.anchor: أن الباطن لا يجب أن يتوصل إليه بالظاهر بل قد يحصل لا بواسطته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers' garden is the garden of witnessing, where audition gives their spirits joy and nourishment; its highest Sufi form comes from the divine presence through sacred spirits and celestial hearing, still resonant with the primordial testimony Am I not your Lord.
rows.anchor: أي يسرون بالسماع في روضة الشهود وذلك غذاء أرواحهم ونعيمها وأعلى أنواع السماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sufis also practice listening to beautiful voices and sounds that stir fear, hope, love, and reverence, including Quran, preaching, drums, reed pipes, strings, flutes, songs, and chants; some are praised and some blameworthy, discussed in detail by Izz al-Din ibn Abd al-Salam.
rows.anchor: وأشتهر عندهم السماع في سماع الأصوات الحسنة وسماع الأشياء المحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evening-and-morning glorification points to filling every moment with God's transcendence and praise; a transmitted saying calls circles of remembrance gardens of Paradise.
rows.anchor: فيه إشارة إلى أنه ينبغي إستغراق الأوقات في تنزيه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bringing forth of the living from the dead alludes to the principle that an offshoot need not resemble its source.
rows.anchor: فيه إشارة إلى أن الفرع لا يلزم أن يكون كأصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An offshoot need not resemble its source: a rose can come from thorns and a narcissus from an onion.
rows.anchor: إنما الورد من الشوك ولا ينبت النرجس إلا من بصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Common kind is one cause of affinity between spouses, as the proverb says birds alight among their likes.
rows.anchor: فيه إشارة إلى أن الإشتراك في الجنسية من أسباب الألفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each party's rejoicing signifies that God does not compel anyone to a state, true or false; souls love according to their readiness, and God gives each lover the beloved suited to that disposition, which is the secret of joy.
rows.anchor: إنه عزوجل لم يكره أحدا على ما هو عليه إن حقا وإن باطلا

rows.speaker: قيس بن ذريح
rows.claim: Qays ibn Dharih's poem portrays souls joined in love before creation and their bond persisting through life, death, and the grave.
rows.anchor: ما ألطف ما قال قيس بن ذريح تعلق روحي روحها قبل خلقنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human nature blends the spirit's guidance and obedience with the lower self's misguidance and disobedience; distress quiets the self and its desires, freeing the spirit to return to God and drawing the self along, but after relief the rebellious nature returns.
rows.anchor: فيها إشارة إلى أن طبيعة الإنسان ممزوجة من هداية الروح وإطاعتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world's corruption signifies that evils are not desired for their own sake, like lancing a wound or cutting an infected finger.
rows.anchor: فيه إشارة إلى أن الشرور ليست مرادة لذاتها بل هي كبط الجرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse instructs heirs of the Muhammadan way and spiritual guides to endure the mockery and contempt of veiled deniers, who reject their states, words, and deeds.
rows.anchor: فيه إشارة لأهل الوراثة المحمدية أهل الإرشاد بأن يصبروا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sura was revealed in Mecca without exception; another report from him exempts three verses, 31:27–29, revealed in Medina after Jewish rabbis challenged the Prophet's statement that human knowledge is little compared with the Torah.
rows.anchor: والبيهقي في الدلائل عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال : أنزلت سورة لقمان بمكة

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: A report from Ata, also cited by al-Dani and Abu Hayyan from Qatada, calls the sura Meccan except for two verses beginning with the parable of trees and pens.
rows.anchor: ونقل الداني عن عطاء وأبو حيان عن قتادة أنهما قالا : هي مكية إلا آيتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes the sura Meccan except for the verse about prayer and zakat because their obligation supposedly began in Medina; the author objects that prayer was prescribed in Mecca on the Night Journey and was at least enjoined there, so this argument fails.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي مكية إلا آية وهي قوله تعالى : ( الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim about prayer and zakat could instead mean both obligations came into force in Medina, even if prayer was already prescribed in Mecca; or zakat may have been prescribed in Mecca, with its taxable thresholds fixed in Medina, which removes the argument.
rows.anchor: فلعل ذلك القائل أراد أن إيجابهما معا تحقق بالمدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura has thirty-three verses in Meccan and Medinan counting systems, and thirty-four in other systems.
rows.anchor: وآيها ثلاث وثلاثون في المكي والمدني وأربع وثلاثون في عدد الباقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: According to al-Bahr, Quraysh asked about Luqman's story with his son and dutifulness to parents, and the sura was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: وسبب نزولها على ما في البحر أن قريشا سألت عن قصة لقمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bahr relates the sura's opening to the preceding statement that the Quran gives every sort of parable, echoed in this sura's opening, and to the earlier challenge to bring a sign, answered by the description of turning away proudly from God's signs.
rows.anchor: ووجه مناسبتها لما قبلها على ما فيه أيضا أنه قال تعالى فيما قبل

rows.speaker: السيوطي
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti connects the two suras through their shared opening letters; Luqman's description of guidance, prayer, zakat, and certainty in the afterlife resumes the prior description of knowledgeable believers who affirm resurrection.
rows.anchor: ظهر لي في إتصالها بما قبلها مع المؤاخاة في الإفتتاح بألمإن قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior sura's believers are in a garden where they rejoice, interpreted as listening, while Luqman's sura begins with idle talk, interpreted as singing and instruments; the author promises a later discussion.
rows.anchor: في روضة يحبرون ) وقد فسر بالسماع وذكر هنا ( ومن الناس من يشتري لهو الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior account of Rome and Persia concerns rulers fighting over a base worldly prize unworthy of a wise person; this sura instead presents Luqman, a wise enslaved man indifferent to worldly life, counseling his son against war and toward patience and peace.
rows.anchor: وما ألطف هذا الإتصال من حيث أن السورة الأولى ذكر فيها مغلوبية الروم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suras also connect in teaching how easy resurrection is: one says God begins and repeats creation, and the other says creating and raising people is like making one soul; both affirm God's hearing and sight.
rows.anchor: فيما تقدم قوله تعالى : ( وهو الذي يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده وهو أهون عليه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The previous sura says some people return to associating partners after hardship, while Luqman says people call upon God alone in storm waves and some later take a moderate course; each sura includes material absent from the other.
rows.anchor: وإذا مس الناس ضر دعوا ربهم منيبين إليه ثم إذا أذاقهم منه رحمة

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari and al-Qutaybi give Luqman's son's name as Taran; other reports give Mathan, An'am, Ashkam, or Mishkam.
rows.anchor: تاران على ما قال الطبري والقتبي وقيل : ماثان بالمثلثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle idh is governed by an omitted command to remember; alternatively it may modify God's grant of wisdom, with omitted words understood from the context.
rows.anchor: معمول لا ذكر محذوفا وقيل : يحتمل أن يكون ظرفا لآتينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase while he was exhorting him is a circumstantial clause; waʿẓ is deterrence joined with warning, or a reminder of good that softens the heart.
rows.anchor: والوعظكما قال الراغبزجر مقترن يتخويف وقال الخليل : هو التذكير بالخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affectionate diminutive ya bunayya expresses compassion and love rather than belittlement, as two cited poems illustrate.
rows.anchor: تصغير إشفاق ومحبة لا تصغير تحقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bazzi reads ya bunayya with a silent yāʾ here, with kasra in a later occurrence and fatḥa in another; a variant gives the same first and third vowels and the middle kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ البزي هنا ( يابني ) بالسكون وفيما بعد ( يابني إنها ) بكسر الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hafs and al-Mufaddal read the three forms with fatḥa, treating the vowel as a substitute for the omitted alif in ya bunayya; the remaining seven readers use kasra.
rows.anchor: وحفص والمفضل عن عاصم بالفتح في الثلاثة على تقدير يابنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Luqman's son was an unbeliever and he warned him until the son converted; a report from al-Fadl al-Raqqashi says Luqman advised him until he died.
rows.anchor: قيل : كان إبنه كافرا ولذا نهاه عن الشرك

rows.speaker: حفص بن عمر الكندي
rows.claim: Hafs ibn Umar al-Kindi tells how Luqman placed mustard seeds in a bag, removing one for each lesson; when it ran out, he said his teaching would split a mountain, and his son wept.
rows.anchor: عن حفص بن عمر الكندي قال : وضع لقمان جرابا من خردل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others say the son and Luqman's wife were already Muslim; the warning against shirk then cautions them against falling into it in future.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان مسلما والنهي عن الشرك تحذير له عن صدوره منه في المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If one pauses after la tushrik, the following bi is an oath particle, making the phrase swear by God that associating partners is a grave wrong.
rows.anchor: ومن وقف على ( لا تشرك ) جعل الباء للقسم أي أقسم بالله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that shirk is a great wrong is most likely Luqman's own speech, as Muslim's Sahih supports; it explains the prohibition because shirk puts things out of place and equates God, the sole giver of blessing, with one who gives none.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا من كلام لقمان ويقتضيه كلام مسلم في صحيحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the declaration is God's own words, detached from Luqman's speech but continuing to reinforce the warning.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو خير من الله تعالى شأنه منقطع عن كلام لقمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parent command is an interjected divine statement reinforcing Luqman's prohibition of shirk; it is not something God said to Luqman.
rows.anchor: كلام مستأنف إعترض به على نهج الإستطراد في أثناء وصية لقمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative makes God say this to Luqman as a further command to be grateful and care for parents; al-Bahr instead attributes the advice to Luqman and says God reports it, but the author dismisses both alternatives.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو من كلامه تعالى قاله جل وعلا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means that God enjoined people to care for their parents.
rows.anchor: والمعنى وأمرنا الإنسان برعاية والديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahnan ala wahn may mean the mother grows increasingly weak as pregnancy progresses toward labor, or it may refer to successive weakness from pregnancy, labor, and postpartum recovery.
rows.anchor: فالمراد تضعف ضعفا متزايدا بإزدياد ثقل الحمل إلى مدة الطلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, wahn may be a circumstantial verbal noun with an implied possessor, an intensified noun used as a circumstantial, or an absolute object of an omitted verb; in the first constructions the clause also describes the mother.
rows.anchor: والمصدر حال من ( أمه ) بتقدير مضاف أي ذات وهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The circumstance may instead describe the child, which accords with Mujahid's report that the child was weak atop the mother's weakness; this avoids the objection that the child's weakness should decrease rather than increase.
rows.anchor: ما أخرجه إبن جرير وإبن أبي حاتم عن مجاهد أنه قال : ( وهنا ) الولد ( على وهن )

rows.speaker: عيسى الثقفي
rows.claim: Isa al-Thaqafi and one transmission from Abu Amr read both instances of wahn with a fatḥa on hāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى الثقفي وأبو عمرو في رواية ( وهنا على وهن ) بفتح الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocalization may reflect the regular Kufa pattern of moving a guttural consonant's vowel, or be the verbal noun of wahina/yawhanu; al-Qamus does not confine either of the two noun forms to a single verb pattern.
rows.anchor: فإن مصدره جاء كذلك وهذا كما يقال تعب يتعب تعبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fiṣāl means weaning and ending suckling; the reading faṣl is broader, while fiṣāl is more apt for nursing despite sharing the same root, as al-Tibi notes.
rows.anchor: وفصاله أي فطامه وترك إرضاعه وقرأ الحسن وأبو رجاء وقتادة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, Abu Raja, Qatada, al-Jahdari, and Yaqub read faṣl in place of fiṣāl.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو رجاء وقتادة والجحدري ويعقوب ( وفصله )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading gives nursing a duration of two years, adopted by al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Abu Yusuf, Muhammad, and al-Tahawi, and reported from Malik.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية أن مدة الرضاع عامان وإلى ذلك ذهب الإمام الشافعي

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa holds that nursing which establishes the legal prohibition lasts thirty months, citing 46:15; he argues that two named periods each receive the full stated duration, by analogy with two debts due in one year or two obligations from one debtor.
rows.anchor: وذهب الإمام أبو حنيفة إلى أن مدة الرضاع الذي يتعلق به التحريم ثلاثون شهرا

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha, whose statement is treated as transmitted from the Prophet, says a child is never in the womb longer than two years, even by the time needed for a spindle's coil; thus gestation is shortened and the explicit nursing term remains, though the author says this needs discussion.
rows.anchor: لقول عائشة الذي لا يقال مثله إلا سماعا : الولد لا يبقى في بطن أمه

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas takes an ishkur li walidayk as an explanatory clause interpreting God's command to care for parents.
rows.anchor: تفسير لوصينا كما أختاره النحاس فإن تفسيرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is a verbal noun with an implied li-taʿlil tied to the command, or a verbal noun in apposition to parents, meaning care for them by gratitude; mentioning gratitude to God comes first because gratitude to parents depends on it, but this last analysis is remote.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن تكون مصدرية بتقدير لام التعليل قبلها وهو متعلق بوصينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that the imperative forbids explanation, rationale, and apposition is invalid; under all three parses, the account from pregnancy through weaning is a parenthetical emphasis on the mother's distinctive burden.
rows.anchor: وعلى الأوجه الثلاثة يكون قوله تعالى : ( حملته أمهإلى عامين ) إعتراضا مؤكدا

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: In a sound report from Bahz ibn Hakim through his father and grandfather, the Prophet names the mother three times when asked whom to honor before naming the father.
rows.anchor: كما في حديث صحيح رواه الترمذي وأبو داؤد عن بهز بن حكيم عن أبيه عن جده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An Arab is said to have carried his mother to pilgrimage on his back while chanting that he carries his mother, who had carried him.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض العرب أنه حمل أمه إلى الحج على ظهره
